title: Orbit Rail: Contextual Navigation & Workspace Paths
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design a reimagined left rail and routing model (the 'Orbit Rail') that reduces cognitive load, surfaces task-specific entry points (dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdowns), and provides a lightweight workspace pathing system for multi-org users. This ticket contains the IA decisions, prototype links, usability findings, and acceptance criteria for the first-phase implementation that will be handed to engineering for a canary rollout.

Goals:
- Provide a single, recognizable anchor (Orbit Rail) that adapts to role and recent task history.
- Enable fast workspace switching and explicit pathing so users can return to a prior context (e.g., "Model -> Canary rollout -> Cost view") without deep menu hunting.
- Surface high-value dashboards (per-route latency/cost) and rollout controls as primary actions rather than buried pages.
- Keep the number of top-level items minimal (7 or fewer) and use progressive disclosure for advanced admin tools.

Scope:
- Left rail IA and new route mapping for Console top-level areas: Home, Models, Endpoints, Rollouts, Observability (dashboards), Billing (cost views), Settings.
- Workspace switcher redesign that preserves recently used contexts and supports keyboard quick-jump.
- Prototypes for desktop (main focus) and tablet breakpoints. Mobile TBD in a follow-up.

Non-goals:
- Full RBAC visual overhaul (only ensure rail labels respect role visibility).
- Backend routing or permission enforcement (ENG will map routes to controllers).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Minimal top-level vs discoverability: Chosen to prioritize minimalism and an ephemeral "tray" that exposes contextual neighbors to reduce top-level clutter. Trade-off: slightly higher discoverability cost for infrequent admin pages.
- Route names: Use task-oriented labels (e.g., "Rollouts") rather than technical nouns ("Canary Manager") to reduce cognitive friction for PMs and non-IR engineers.
- Workspace paths: Persist the last 3 contexted paths per workspace; this reduces memory reliance while keeping the rail lightweight. We considered full session history but rejected it due to clutter and privacy concerns.
- Keyboard-first interactions: All primary rail items map to single-key shortcuts (e.g., G then R -> go to Rollouts). This adds a small learning curve but dramatically improves power-user efficiency.

Accessibility notes:
- Focus outlines preserved for keyboard nav; new tray uses ARIA regions to announce context changes; contrast ratios verified against WCAG AA.

Deliverables attached to this ticket:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype (primary flows)
- Interactive InVision clickable for developer handoff
- Design tokens and updated component spec for the left rail (color, spacing, collapsed state)
- Usability test notes (8 participants, engineers and PMs)

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in time-to-first-action for rollout-related tasks in the next sprint of GA telemetry.
- 15% reduction in support tickets about "where is X" for rollouts and cost pages.
- Positive qualitative feedback in usability tests (median SUS increase of 6 points for navigation tasks).
acceptance_criteria: Left rail implements Orbit grouping with 7 or fewer top-level items
Workspace switcher surfaces last 3 context paths and supports keyboard quick-jump
Rollouts and Cost pages are discoverable from primary rail and have direct deep-links
ARIA roles and keyboard focus tested and documented
Design tokens committed to design-system repo and linked PR merged
